title.zh: 卷四十 志第二十: 地理三
title.raw: 卷四十 志第二十: 地理三 Volume 40 Treatises 20: Geography 3

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 志第二十四職官三御史臺御史臺秦、漢曰御史府，後漢改為憲臺，魏、晉、宋改為蘭臺，梁、陳、北朝咸曰御史臺。

translations.literal: Treatise 24, Offices and Ranks 3: The Censorate. The Censorate: Under Qin and Han it was called the Bureau of Censors; in Later Han it was changed to the Chancellery of Censors; under Wei, Jin, and Song it was changed to the Orchid Terrace; under Liang, Chen, and the Northern dynasties it was uniformly called the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 24, Offices and Ranks, Part 3 — the Censorate. In Qin and Han times the office was known as the Bureau of Censors; Later Han renamed it the Chancellery of Censors; Wei, Jin, and Song called it the Orchid Terrace; Liang, Chen, and the Northern dynasties all used the name Censorate.

sentences.zh: 武德因之。

translations.literal: Wude adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude the same arrangement was kept.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改名憲臺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo its name was changed to the Chancellery of Censors.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo year 2 it was renamed the Chancellery of Censors.

sentences.zh: 咸亨復。

translations.literal: Xianheng restored it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianheng era restored the former name.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年分臺為左右，號曰左右肅政臺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai the Censorate was divided into left and right, styled the Left and Right Offices of Rectifying Government.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzhai year 1 the bureau was split into left and right sections, called the Left and Right Offices of Rectifying Government.

sentences.zh: 左臺專知京百司，右臺按察諸州。

translations.literal: The left office had exclusive charge of the hundred offices of the capital; the right office inspected the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The left bureau supervised all capital ministries; the right bureau conducted inspections in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 神龍復為左右御史臺。

translations.literal: Shenlong again made them the Left and Right Censorates.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong period they were again styled the Left and Right Censorates.

sentences.zh: 延和年廢右臺，先天二年復置，十月又廢也。

translations.literal: In the Yanhe period the right Censorate was abolished; in the second year of Xiantian it was re-established, and in the tenth month it was abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: The right Censorate was abolished in the Yanhe period; it was restored in Xiantian year 2 and abolished again in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫大夫一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief: one post, upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief — one position, upper third rank.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢之制，御史大夫、副丞相為三公之官。

translations.literal: Under the Qin and Han systems, the Censor-in-Chief, as deputy to the Chancellor, was an office of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin and Han practice the Censor-in-Chief served as the Chancellor's deputy and ranked among the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之後，多不置大夫，以中丞為臺主。

translations.literal: After Wei and Jin, the post of Chief was often not filled; the Vice Censor was made head of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei and Jin the chief post was often left vacant, and the Vice Censor served as head of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 隋諱中，復大夫，降為正四品。

translations.literal: Sui avoided the character zhong, restored the Chief, and reduced the rank to upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the taboo character zhong, Sui restored the Chief but lowered the rank to upper fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》改為從三品。

translations.literal: The Wude Statutes changed it to lower third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Statutes set the rank at lower third grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為大司憲，咸亨復為大夫。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed the title to Grand Director of Censors; Xianheng restored the title Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo it became Grand Director of Censors; Xianheng restored the title Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 光宅分臺為左、右，置左、右臺大夫。

translations.literal: Guangzhai divided the Censorate into left and right and established Chiefs of the Left and Right Censorates.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangzhai period the bureau was split into left and right, each with its own Chief.

sentences.zh: 及廢右臺，去「左」「右」字。

translations.literal: When the right Censorate was abolished, the words "left" and "right" were dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After the right bureau was abolished, the designations "left" and "right" were removed.

sentences.zh: 本從三品，會昌二年十二月敕：「大夫，秦為正卿，漢為副相，漢末改為大司空，與丞相俱為三公。

translations.literal: Originally lower third rank. An edict of the twelfth month of the second year of Huichang: "The Chief: in Qin he was a chief minister; in Han he was deputy chancellor; at the end of Han he was changed to Grand Minister of Works, and together with the Chancellor he formed the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been lower third rank. A Huichang year 2, twelfth-month edict stated: "The Censor-in-Chief: in Qin he ranked as a chief minister; in Han as deputy chancellor; at the end of Han the title became Grand Minister of Works, sharing with the Chancellor the status of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 掌邦國刑憲，肅正朝廷。

translations.literal: He held charge of the state's penal statutes and rectified the court.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the state's penal code and kept the court in order.

sentences.zh: 其任既重，品秩宜峻。

translations.literal: Since his responsibility is weighty, his rank ought to be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the duties are weighty, the rank should be correspondingly high.

sentences.zh: 准六尚書例，升為正三品，著之於令。

translations.literal: Following the precedent of the six Ministers, he is promoted to upper third rank and this is written into the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of the six Ministers, the rank is raised to upper third grade and recorded in the statutes.

sentences.zh: 」中丞二員。

translations.literal: " Vice Censors: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Censors — two posts.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Lower upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower upper fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 漢御史臺有二丞，掌殿內秘書，謂之中丞。

translations.literal: The Han Censorate had two Vice Directors who managed palace documents and were called Vice Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Han had two vice directors on the Censorate who handled palace documents and were known as Vice Censors.

sentences.zh: 漢末改為御史長史，後漢復為中丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Han it was changed to Chief Secretary of the Censors; Later Han restored the title Vice Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han renamed the post Chief Secretary of the Censors; Later Han restored the title Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 後魏改為中尉正，北齊復曰中丞。

translations.literal: Later Wei changed it to Director of the Inner Guard; Northern Qi again called it Vice Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei styled it Director of the Inner Guard; Northern Qi again used Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 後周曰司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: Later Zhou called it Director of Censors, middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou titled it Director of Censors, middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 隋諱中，改為持書御史，為從五品。

translations.literal: Sui avoided zhong and changed the title to Censor Holding Documents, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, avoiding the taboo, renamed the post Censor Holding Documents at lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 武德因之。

translations.literal: Wude adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude the same title and rank were kept.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，避高宗名，改持書御史為中丞，置二員。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan, to avoid the Gaozong taboo, Censor Holding Documents was changed back to Vice Censor, and two posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenguan, to avoid Emperor Gaozong's taboo name, the title reverted to Vice Censor and two posts were created.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司憲大夫，咸亨復為中丞。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to Director of Censors; Xianheng restored Vice Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Director of Censors; Xianheng restored Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 本正五品上，會昌二年十二月敕：「中丞為大夫之貳，緣大夫秩崇，官不常置，中丞為憲臺長。

translations.literal: Originally upper fifth rank. Edict of the twelfth month of Huichang year 2: "The Vice Censor is second to the Chief; because the Chief's rank is exalted the post is not always filled, and the Vice Censor is head of the Chancellery of Censors.
translations.idiomatic: The rank had been upper fifth grade. A Huichang year 2, twelfth-month edict read: "The Vice Censor is deputy to the Chief; because the Chief's rank is lofty the post is not always occupied, and the Vice Censor serves as head of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 今九寺少卿及諸少監、國子司業、京兆少尹，並府寺省監之貳，皆為四品，唯中丞官重，品秩未崇，可升為正四品下，與丞郎出入迭用，著之於令。

translations.literal: Now the Vice Directors of the nine Directorates, the various Vice Superintendents, the Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, the Vice Governor of Jingzhao, and all deputies of directorates, offices, and ministries are fourth rank; only the Vice Censor's office is weighty yet his rank is not exalted — he may be promoted to lower upper fourth rank, alternating in and out of service with Directors and Gentlemen, and this is written into the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Today the vice directors of the nine directorates, various vice superintendents, the vice chancellor of the Directorate of Education, the vice governor of Jingzhao, and other second-rank posts in ministries and offices are all fourth grade; only the Vice Censor's duties are weighty while his rank remains low — let it be raised to lower upper fourth grade, used interchangeably with directors and gentlemen, and entered in the statutes.

sentences.zh: 」大夫、中丞之職，掌持邦國刑憲典章，以肅正朝廷。

translations.literal: " The duties of the Chief and Vice Censor are to uphold the state's penal statutes and regulations and thereby rectify the court.
translations.idiomatic: " The Chief and Vice Censor uphold the state's penal code and regulations to keep the court in order.

sentences.zh: 中丞為之貳。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Censor serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之人，有稱冤而無告者，與三司訊之。

translations.literal: Whenever people throughout the realm claim injustice yet have no one to whom they may appeal, they are examined together with the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone in the realm who claims injustice but has no recourse is examined jointly with the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百僚之事，應彈劾者，御史言于大夫。

translations.literal: In all matters of inner and outer officials that warrant impeachment, the censor reports to the Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an inner or outer official should be impeached, the censor reports to the Chief.

sentences.zh: 大事則方幅奏彈之，小事則署名而已。

translations.literal: Major cases are memorialized and impeached in full form; minor cases require only a signature.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases are submitted as formal impeachments; minor ones need only a signature.

sentences.zh: 若有制使覆囚徒，則與刑部尚書參擇之。

translations.literal: If an imperial commissioner reviews prisoners, he deliberates jointly with the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial commissioner reviews prisoners, he does so together with the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 凡國有大禮，則乘輅車以為之導。

translations.literal: Whenever the state holds a great ceremony, he rides the state carriage to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: At major state ceremonies he rides the ceremonial carriage as escort.

sentences.zh: 侍御史侍御史四員。

translations.literal: Attending Censor: four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor — four posts.

sentences.zh: 從六品下。

translations.literal: Lower sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 御史之名，《周官》有之，亦名柱下史。

translations.literal: The name censor appears in the Offices of Zhou and was also called Secretary under the Pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The title censor appears in the Offices of Zhou and was also known as Secretary under the Pillar.

sentences.zh: 秦改為侍御史。

translations.literal: Qin changed it to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Qin renamed the post Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 後周曰司憲中士，隋為侍御史，品第七。

translations.literal: Later Zhou called it Director of Censors, middle gentleman; Sui made it Attending Censor, seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou styled it Director of Censors, middle gentleman; under Sui it was Attending Censor, seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 武德品第六也。

translations.literal: Under Wude it was sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude it was sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌糾舉百僚，推鞫獄訟。

translations.literal: He is in charge of impeaching officials and investigating legal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He impeaches officials and investigates lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 侍御史年深者一人判臺事，知公廨雜事，次一人知西推，一人知東推也。

translations.literal: One senior Attending Censor adjudicates Censorate business and handles miscellaneous office affairs; next, one manages the western investigation, and one manages the eastern investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The senior Attending Censor adjudicates bureau affairs and handles routine office business; another oversees the western docket and another the eastern docket.

sentences.zh: 凡有別付推者，則按其實狀以奏。

translations.literal: Whenever a case is separately assigned for investigation, he reports according to the actual facts.
translations.idiomatic: Cases specially assigned for investigation are reported on the basis of the facts.

sentences.zh: 若尋常之獄，推訖斷於大理。

translations.literal: If it is an ordinary case, after investigation judgment rests with the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary cases, once investigated, are decided by the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 凡事非大夫、中丞所劾，而合彈奏者，則具其事為狀，大夫、中丞押奏。

translations.literal: In all matters not impeached by the Chief or Vice Censor but warranting impeachment, the facts are set out in a memorial and the Chief and Vice Censor countersign the submission.
translations.idiomatic: Matters requiring impeachment that were not raised by the Chief or Vice Censor are memorialized in full and submitted under their countersignatures.

sentences.zh: 大事則冠法冠，衣硃衣纁裳，白紗中單以彈之。

translations.literal: For major cases he wears the law cap, vermilion upper garment and brown lower garment, and white gauze undershirt to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: For major impeachments he dons the law cap, vermilion coat, brown skirt, and white gauze undershirt.

sentences.zh: 小事常服而已。

translations.literal: For minor cases ordinary dress suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Minor cases require only ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 凡三司理事，則與給事中、中書舍人更直，直於朝堂受表。

translations.literal: Whenever the Three Offices hear cases, he rotates duty with the Attendant within the Gates and the Secretariat Drafter, keeping watch in the court hall to receive petitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Offices hear cases, he alternates duty with the Attendant within the Gates and the Secretariat drafter, receiving petitions in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 若三司所按而非其長官，則與刑部郎中員外、大理司直評事往訊之。

translations.literal: If the Three Offices investigate someone other than his immediate superior, he goes with the Director and Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and the Reviewing Clerk and Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review to conduct the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: If the Three Offices investigate someone below their own chief, he joins the Ministry of Justice directors and the Court of Judicial Review clerks on the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 主簿、錄事主簿一人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Registrar and Recorder: one Registrar, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar and Recorder — one Registrar, lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 錄事二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Two Recorders, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Recorders, lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 主簿掌印及受事發辰，勾檢稽失。

translations.literal: The Registrar holds the seal, receives documents and issues time-stamps, and checks for omissions and errors.
translations.idiomatic: The Registrar keeps the seal, receives documents, timestamps them, and audits for lapses.

sentences.zh: 兼知官廚及黃卷。

translations.literal: He also oversees the official kitchen and the yellow-bound archives.
translations.idiomatic: He also supervises the office kitchen and the yellow-bound archives.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，令史十七人，書令史二十三人。

translations.literal: Two Clerks, seventeen Clerks of Records, and twenty-three Clerks for Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks, seventeen record clerks, and twenty-three document clerks.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史殿中侍御史六人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Palace Attending Censor: six posts, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attending Censor — six posts, lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 令史八人，書令史十八人。

translations.literal: Eight Clerks of Records and eighteen Clerks for Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Eight record clerks and eighteen document clerks.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史掌殿廷供奉之儀式。

translations.literal: The Palace Attending Censor is in charge of ceremonial attendance in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attending Censors supervise ceremonial attendance in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 凡冬至、元正大朝會，則具服升殿。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice and New Year's grand audiences he dons full dress and ascends the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice and New Year grand audiences they wear full court dress and enter the hall.

sentences.zh: 若郊祀、巡幸，則於鹵簿中糾察非違，具服從於旌門，視文物有所虧闕，則糾之。

translations.literal: If there is suburban sacrifice or an imperial tour, he inspects for improprieties within the guard of honor, wears full dress and follows at the banner gate, and if regalia is deficient he corrects it.
translations.idiomatic: On suburban sacrifices or imperial tours they inspect the guard of honor for breaches, follow in full dress at the banner gate, and correct any deficiency in regalia.

sentences.zh: 凡兩京城內，則分知左右巡，各察其所巡之內有不法之事。

translations.literal: Within the two capitals they divide charge of left and right patrols, each inspecting unlawful conduct within his patrol district.
translations.idiomatic: In the two capitals they split left and right patrols, each investigating illegal conduct in his sector.

sentences.zh: 監察御史監察御史十員，正八品上。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor: ten posts, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor — ten posts, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，馬周以布衣進用，大宗令于監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, Ma Zhou was advanced from commoner status and Taizong ordered him to serve as acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan Ma Zhou, though still a commoner, was promoted at Taizong's order to serve as acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 自此因置裏行之名。

translations.literal: From this the title of acting status was established.
translations.idiomatic: From this the designation "acting" was introduced.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，以王本立為監察裏行也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo, Wang Benli was made acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo year 1 Wang Benli was appointed acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 監察掌分察巡按郡縣、屯田、鑄錢、嶺南選補、知太府、司農出納，監決囚徒。

translations.literal: Investigating Censors are in charge of divided inspection and touring of prefectures and counties, garrison colonies, coinage, Lingnan selection and appointment, oversight of the Grand Storehouse and the Directorate of Agriculture's receipts and disbursements, and supervision of prisoners' sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors inspect prefectures and counties, garrison farms, mints, and Lingnan appointments; oversee the Grand Storehouse and Directorate of Agriculture accounts; and supervise sentencing of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 監祭祀則閱牲牢，省器服，不敬則劾祭官。

translations.literal: When supervising sacrifices he inspects the livestock pens, examines vessels and vestments, and if there is irreverence impeaches the sacrificial officer.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices they inspect livestock, examine vessels and robes, and impeach sacrificial officers for irreverence.

sentences.zh: 尚書省有會議，亦監其過謬。

translations.literal: When the Department of State Affairs holds conferences, he also supervises their errors.
translations.idiomatic: They also monitor Department of State Affairs conferences for errors.

sentences.zh: 凡百官宴會、習射，亦如之。

translations.literal: The same applies to banquets and archery practice of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to official banquets and archery drills.

sentences.zh: 殿中省殿中省魏初置殿中監，隋初改為殿中局，煬帝改為殿內省，武德改為殿中省。

translations.literal: Palace Department. Palace Department: Wei at first established the Palace Superintendent; early Sui changed it to the Palace Bureau; Emperor Yang changed it to the Inner Palace Department; Wude changed it to the Palace Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Department. Wei first created the Palace Superintendent; early Sui renamed it the Palace Bureau; Emperor Yang made it the Inner Palace Department; Wude restored the name Palace Department.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為中御府，咸亨復為殿中省。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to the Central Imperial Household Office; Xianheng restored the Palace Department.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it the Central Imperial Household Office; Xianheng restored the Palace Department.

sentences.zh: 監一員，從三品。

translations.literal: Superintendent: one post, lower third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent — one post, lower third rank.

sentences.zh: 魏初置，品第二。

translations.literal: Established at the beginning of Wei, second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Created early in Wei at second grade.

sentences.zh: 梁品第三。

translations.literal: Liang: third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, third grade.

sentences.zh: 隋品第四。

translations.literal: Sui: fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 武德品第三也。

translations.literal: Under Wude: third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude, third grade.

sentences.zh: 少監二員，從四品上。

translations.literal: Two Vice Superintendents, upper lower fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Vice Superintendents, upper lower fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Two Directors, upper lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors, upper lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two Clerks, upper lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks, upper lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史十二人，亭長、掌固各八人。

translations.literal: Four Clerks of Records, twelve Clerks for Documents, and eight Station Chiefs and eight Custodians each.
translations.idiomatic: Four record clerks, twelve document clerks, and eight station chiefs and eight custodians.

sentences.zh: 殿中監掌天子服御，總領尚食、尚藥、尚衣、尚舍、尚舍、尚輦六局之官屬，備其禮物，供其職事。

translations.literal: The Palace Superintendent is in charge of the Son of Heaven's apparel and equipage, and generally directs the officials of the six bureaus — Food, Medicine, Garments, Lodging, Lodging, and Carriages — preparing their ritual objects and supplying their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Superintendent oversees the emperor's apparel and equipage and directs the six bureaus — Food, Medicine, Garments, Lodging, and Carriages — providing their ritual goods and supplies.

sentences.zh: 少監為之貳。

translations.literal: The Vice Superintendent is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Superintendent serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡聽朝，則率其屬執傘扇以列於左右。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor holds court, he leads his subordinates bearing umbrellas and fans to array left and right.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences he leads subordinates bearing umbrellas and fans to stand left and right.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀，則進大珪、鎮珪於壝門之外。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices he presents the great jade tablet and the stabilizing jade tablet outside the spirit gate.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices he presents the great and stabilizing jade tablets outside the spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 既事，受而藏之。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, he receives them and stores them away.
translations.idiomatic: After the rite he receives and stores them.

sentences.zh: 凡行幸，則侍奉於仗內，驂乘以從。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses he attends within the guard of honor and follows in the outrider carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours he attends within the guard and follows in the outrider carriage.

sentences.zh: 若元正、冬至大朝會，則有進爵之禮。

translations.literal: At the New Year and winter solstice grand audiences there is the ceremony of presenting the wine cup.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year and winter solstice grand audiences they perform the ceremony of presenting the wine cup.

sentences.zh: 丞掌副監事，兼勾檢稽失，省署抄目。

translations.literal: The Director assists the Vice Superintendent in affairs, and also checks for omissions and errors and reviews office copies and registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Director assists the Vice Superintendent, audits for lapses, and reviews office registers.

sentences.zh: 主事掌印及知受事發辰。

translations.literal: The Clerk holds the seal and knows how to receive documents and issue time-stamps.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk keeps the seal and timestamps incoming documents.

sentences.zh: 尚食局尚食局：奉御二人，正五品下。

translations.literal: Food Bureau. Food Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, lower upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Food Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, lower upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 隋初為典御，又改為奉御。

translations.literal: Early Sui called them Directors of the Imperial Kitchen; later they were changed to Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui titled them Directors of the Imperial Kitchen; later they became Imperial Attendants.

sentences.zh: 直長五人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Five Chief Stewards, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five Chief Stewards, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 食醫八人。

translations.literal: Eight Dietary Physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Eight dietary physicians.

sentences.zh: 正九品下。

translations.literal: Lower upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌謹其儲供，辨名數。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of carefully managing stored provisions and distinguishing names and quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants carefully manage stored provisions and keep accounts of names and quantities.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 若進御，必辨其時禁。

translations.literal: If presented to the emperor, seasonal prohibitions must be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When food is presented to the emperor, seasonal dietary prohibitions must be observed.

sentences.zh: 春肝，夏心，秋肺，冬腎，四季之月脾王，皆不可食。

translations.literal: In spring the liver, in summer the heart, in autumn the lung, in winter the kidney; in the months of the four seasons when the spleen is sovereign — all may not be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: In spring liver is forbidden, in summer heart, in autumn lung, and in winter kidney; in the intercalary months of the four seasons, when the spleen dominates, all of these are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 當進，必先嘗。

translations.literal: When about to be presented, it must first be tasted.
translations.idiomatic: Before presentation, it must first be tasted.

sentences.zh: 正、至大朝會饗宴，與光祿大夫視其品秩之差。

translations.literal: At New Year and winter solstice grand audiences and banquets, together with the Masters of the Bright Capital they observe the differences in rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year and winter solstice grand audiences and banquets, they work with the Masters of the Bright Capital to allocate provisions according to rank.

sentences.zh: 其賜王公賓客，亦如之。

translations.literal: Grants to princes, nobles, and guests follow the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to provisions granted to princes, nobles, and guests.

sentences.zh: 諸陵月享，則視膳而獻之。

translations.literal: For the monthly offerings at the imperial tombs, they inspect the ritual food and present it.
translations.idiomatic: For monthly offerings at the imperial tombs, they inspect the ritual food and present it.

sentences.zh: 食醫掌率主食王膳，以供其職。

translations.literal: Dietary physicians are in charge of leading those who prepare the imperial meals to fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Dietary physicians lead those who prepare the imperial meals in fulfillment of their duties.

sentences.zh: 尚藥局尚藥局：奉御二人，正五品下。

translations.literal: Pharmaceutical Bureau. Pharmaceutical Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, lower upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pharmaceutical Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, lower upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 直長四人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Four Chief Stewards, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four Chief Stewards, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 書吏四人。

translations.literal: Four clerical officers.
translations.idiomatic: Four clerical officers.

sentences.zh: 侍御醫四人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Four Attending Imperial Physicians, upper subordinate sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four Attending Imperial Physicians, upper subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 主藥十二人，藥童三十人。

translations.literal: Twelve chief pharmacists and thirty pharmacy apprentices.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve chief pharmacists and thirty pharmacy apprentices.

sentences.zh: 司醫四人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Four Bureau Physicians, lower upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four Bureau Physicians, lower upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 醫佐八人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Eight medical assistants, lower upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eight medical assistants, lower upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 按摩師四人，咒禁師四人，合口脂匠四人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Four masseurs, four incantation specialists, four lip-balm compounders, and four storeroom keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Four masseurs, four incantation specialists, four lip-balm compounders, and four storeroom keepers.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌合和御藥及診候方脈之事。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of compounding imperial medicines and examining pulses according to prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants manage compounding imperial medicines and pulse diagnosis according to prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡藥有上、中、下三品，上藥為君，中藥為臣，下藥為佐。

translations.literal: In general medicines have upper, middle, and lower three grades; upper medicines serve as sovereign, middle medicines as minister, and lower medicines as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Medicines are divided into upper, middle, and lower grades: upper medicines serve as the sovereign drug, middle medicines as ministers, and lower medicines as adjutants.

sentences.zh: 合造之法，一君三臣九佐，別入五藏，分其五味。

translations.literal: The method of compounding is one sovereign, three ministers, and nine adjutants, separately entering the five viscera and dividing the five flavors.
translations.idiomatic: The compounding formula calls for one sovereign drug, three minister drugs, and nine adjutant drugs, each assigned to the five viscera and distributed among the five flavors.

sentences.zh: 有湯丸膏散之用。

translations.literal: There are uses of decoctions, pills, ointments, and powders.
translations.idiomatic: They are prepared as decoctions, pills, ointments, and powders.

sentences.zh: 診脈有寸、關、尺之三部，醫之大經。

translations.literal: Pulse diagnosis has the three positions of cun, guan, and chi — the great canon of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Pulse diagnosis employs the three positions of cun, guan, and chi — the fundamental canon of medicine.

sentences.zh: 凡合和與監視其分劑，藥成嘗而進焉。

translations.literal: In all compounding and supervising proportions, when the medicine is ready it is tasted and then presented.
translations.idiomatic: They compound medicines, supervise dosages, taste each preparation when finished, and then present it.

sentences.zh: 侍御醫，掌診候調和。

translations.literal: Attending Imperial Physicians manage diagnosis and harmonizing prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Imperial Physicians manage diagnosis and prescription harmonization.

sentences.zh: 主藥、藥童，主刮削搗簁。

translations.literal: Chief pharmacists and pharmacy apprentices are in charge of scraping, pounding, and sifting.
translations.idiomatic: Chief pharmacists and pharmacy apprentices scrape, pound, and sift the ingredients.

sentences.zh: 尚衣局尚衣局：奉御二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Garment Bureau. Garment Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Garment Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 直長四人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Four Chief Stewards, lower upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four Chief Stewards, lower upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 書令史三人，書吏四人，主衣十六人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Three chief clerks, four clerical officers, sixteen garment stewards, and four storeroom keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Three chief clerks, four clerical officers, sixteen garment stewards, and four storeroom keepers.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌衣服，詳其制度，辨其名數。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of garments, detailing their regulations and distinguishing names and quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants manage imperial garments, specify their regulations, and keep accounts of names and quantities.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡天子之服冕十有三；

translations.literal: In all, the Son of Heaven's caps and robes number thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's ritual caps and robes number thirteen in all.

sentences.zh: 一，大裘冕，二袞冕，一鷩冕，四毳冕，五黻冕，六玄冕，七通天冠，八武弁，九弁服，十介幘，十一白紗帽，十二平巾幘，十三翼善冠。

translations.literal: First, the Grand Fur Cap and Robe; second, the Emblem Cap and Robe; third, the Pheasant Cap and Robe; fourth, the Feather Cap and Robe; fifth, the Brocade Cap and Robe; sixth, the Dark Cap and Robe; seventh, the Heaven-Penetrating Cap; eighth, the Martial Cap; ninth, the Cap and Robe; tenth, the Bound Headcloth; eleventh, the White Gauze Cap; twelfth, the Level Headcloth; thirteenth, the Good-Wings Cap.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Grand Fur Cap and Robe; second, the Emblem Cap and Robe; third, the Pheasant Cap and Robe; fourth, the Feather Cap and Robe; fifth, the Brocade Cap and Robe; sixth, the Dark Cap and Robe; seventh, the Heaven-Penetrating Cap; eighth, the Martial Cap; ninth, the Cap and Robe; tenth, the Bound Headcloth; eleventh, the White Gauze Cap; twelfth, the Level Headcloth; and thirteenth, the Good-Wings Cap.

sentences.zh: 事具《輿服志》。

translations.literal: The details are fully given in the 《Treatise on Carriages and Vestments》.
translations.idiomatic: Full particulars are given in the 《Treatise on Carriages and Vestments》.

sentences.zh: 凡天子之大珪，曰珽，長三尺。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's great jade tablet, called ting, is three feet long.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's great jade tablet, called ting, measures three feet in length.

sentences.zh: 鎮珪，長尺有二寸。

translations.literal: The stabilizing jade tablet is one foot and two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The stabilizing jade tablet is one foot and two inches long.

sentences.zh: 若有事於郊丘社稷，則出之於內。

translations.literal: If there are rites at the suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain, it is taken out from the inner store.
translations.idiomatic: When rites are performed at the suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain, the tablet is taken from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 將享，至於中壝門，則奉鎮珪於監而進之。

translations.literal: When about to perform the sacrifice, upon reaching the middle enclosure gate, the stabilizing jade tablet is presented on a tray and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice is about to begin, upon reaching the middle enclosure gate, they present the stabilizing jade tablet on a ceremonial tray and advance it.

sentences.zh: 既事，受而藏之。

translations.literal: When the rite is complete, it is received and stored away.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is finished, they receive the tablet and store it away.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會，則設案，服畢而徹之。

translations.literal: At all grand audiences, a stand is set out; when dressing is complete, it is removed.
translations.idiomatic: At grand audiences, a display stand is set out for the robes and removed once dressing is complete.

sentences.zh: 尚舍局尚舍局：奉御二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Lodging Bureau. Lodging Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 直工六人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Six Chief Artisans, lower upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Six Chief Artisans, lower upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 書令史三人，書吏七人，掌固十人，幕士八十人。

translations.literal: Three chief clerks, seven clerical officers, ten storeroom keepers, and eighty tent bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Three chief clerks, seven clerical officers, ten storeroom keepers, and eighty tent bearers.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌殿廷張設、湯沐、燈燭、灑掃之事。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of palace hall arrangements, hot water for bathing, lamps and candles, and sprinkling and sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants manage palace hall arrangements, bathing supplies, lamps and candles, and cleaning.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡行幸，預設三部帳幕，有古帳、大帳、次帳、小次帳、小帳，凡五等之帳為三部。

translations.literal: On imperial progress, three sets of tent curtains are preset in advance; there are the ancient tent, great tent, secondary tent, small secondary tent, and small tent — five grades of tents forming three sets.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, three sets of tent curtains are prepared in advance, comprising five grades — ancient tent, great tent, secondary tent, small secondary tent, and small tent — arranged as three sections.

sentences.zh: 其外置排城以為蔽扞。

translations.literal: Outside, palisade walls are set up as protective shields.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the tents, palisade walls are erected as protective barriers.

sentences.zh: 排城，連板為之，板上畫辟邪獸，表裏皆漆之。

translations.literal: Palisade walls are made by joining boards; beasts warding off evil are painted on the boards, lacquered inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Palisade walls are built of joined boards painted with beasts warding off evil and lacquered on both sides.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀，有事於郊壇，則先設行宮于壇之東南向，隨地之宜，將祀三日，則設大次於外壝東門之外道北，南向而設坐。

translations.literal: At all major sacrifices, when rites are performed at the suburban altar, a traveling palace is first set up southeast of the altar according to local conditions; three days before the sacrifice, the great tent is set up north of the road outside the outer enclosure's east gate, facing south with seats arranged.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices performed at the suburban altar, a traveling palace is first erected southeast of the altar as terrain permits; three days before the rite, the great tent is set up north of the road outside the outer enclosure's east gate, facing south with seats in place.

sentences.zh: 若有事於明堂太廟，則設大次於東門，如郊壇之制。

translations.literal: If rites are performed at the Bright Hall and Imperial Ancestral Temple, the great tent is set up at the east gate, following the suburban altar regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When rites are performed at the Bright Hall and Imperial Ancestral Temple, the great tent is set up at the east gate according to the same regulations used at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 凡致齋則設幄於正殿西序及室內，俱東向，張於楹下。

translations.literal: When observing fasting purification, curtains are set up in the west wing of the main hall and within the chambers, all facing east and hung beneath the pillars.
translations.idiomatic: During fasting purification, curtains are hung beneath the pillars in the west wing of the main hall and in the inner chambers, all facing east.

sentences.zh: 凡元正、冬至大朝會，則設斧扆於正殿。

translations.literal: At New Year and winter solstice grand audiences, an axe-back screen is set up in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year and winter solstice grand audiences, an axe-back screen is installed in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 施蹋席薰爐。

translations.literal: Treading mats and censers are laid out.
translations.idiomatic: Treading mats and censers are placed in position.

sentences.zh: 朔望受朝，則施幄於正殿，帳裙頂帶，方闊一丈四尺也。

translations.literal: At new- and full-moon audiences, curtains are hung in the main hall; the curtain skirt and top band span one zhang and four chi square.
translations.idiomatic: At new- and full-moon audiences, curtains are hung in the main hall, with skirt and top band measuring one zhang and four chi square.

sentences.zh: 尚乘局尚乘局：奉御二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Horse Bureau. Horse Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Horse Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 直長一人，正七品下。

translations.literal: One Chief Steward, lower upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Steward, lower upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 奉乘十八人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Eighteen Imperial Carriage Attendants, lower upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen Imperial Carriage Attendants, lower upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 習馭五十人，掌閑五十人，獸醫七十人。

translations.literal: Fifty horse trainers, fifty stable keepers, and seventy veterinarians.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty horse trainers, fifty stable keepers, and seventy veterinarians.

sentences.zh: 進馬六人，七品下。

translations.literal: Six Presenting-Horse officers, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Six Presenting-Horse officers, lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 司庫一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: One Storehouse Keeper, lower upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Storehouse Keeper, lower upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 司廩二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Two Granary Keepers, lower upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Granary Keepers, lower upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 書令史一人，書吏十四人。

translations.literal: One chief clerk and fourteen clerical officers.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk and fourteen clerical officers.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌內外閑廄之馬，辨其粗良，而率其習馭。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of horses of the inner and outer leisurely stables, distinguishes coarse from fine, and leads the horse trainers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants manage the horses of the inner and outer imperial stables, distinguish quality grades, and supervise the horse trainers.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 一曰左右飛黃閑，二曰左右吉良閑，三曰左右龍媒閑，四曰左右抃駼閑，五曰左右駃騠閑，六曰左右天苑閑。

translations.literal: First, the Left and Right Flying Yellow Leisure [Studs]; second, the Left and Right Auspicious Fine Leisure [Studs]; third, the Left and Right Dragon Matchmaker Leisure [Studs]; fourth, the Left and Right Biantu Leisure [Studs]; fifth, the Left and Right Swift Hybrid Leisure [Studs]; sixth, the Left and Right Heavenly Park Leisure [Studs].
translations.idiomatic: First, the Left and Right Flying Yellow studs; second, the Left and Right Auspicious Fine studs; third, the Left and Right Dragon Matchmaker studs; fourth, the Left and Right Biantu studs; fifth, the Left and Right Swift Hybrid studs; and sixth, the Left and Right Heavenly Park studs.

sentences.zh: 開元時仗內六閑，曰飛龍、祥麟、鳳苑、鵷鶵、吉良、六群等，號六廄馬。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period the six leisure [studs] within the guard of honor were called Flying Dragon, Auspicious Unicorn, Phoenix Park, Yuanchu, Auspicious Fine, and Six Herds, styled the Six Stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the six inner guard studs were named Flying Dragon, Auspicious Unicorn, Phoenix Park, Yuanchu, Auspicious Fine, and Six Herds — known as the Six Stable horses.

sentences.zh: 凡秣馬給料，以時為差。

translations.literal: For feeding horses and allotting fodder, differences are made according to season.
translations.idiomatic: Feed and fodder allotments for horses vary according to the season.

sentences.zh: 凡外牧進良馬，印以三花飛風之字而為志。

translations.literal: When outer pastures present fine horses, they are marked with the seal of the characters "three flowers flying wind" as identification.
translations.idiomatic: Fine horses presented from outer pastures are branded with the "three flowers flying wind" mark for identification.

sentences.zh: 奉乘掌率習馭、掌閑、駕士及秣飼之法。

translations.literal: Imperial Carriage Attendants are in charge of leading horse trainers, stable keepers, charioteers, and the methods of feeding.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Carriage Attendants supervise horse trainers, stable keepers, and charioteers, and regulate feeding practices.

sentences.zh: 司庫掌鞍轡乘具。

translations.literal: The Storehouse Keeper is in charge of saddles, bridles, and riding equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The Storehouse Keeper manages saddles, bridles, and riding equipment.

sentences.zh: 司廩掌槁秸出納。

translations.literal: The Granary Keeper is in charge of issuing and receiving straw and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Keeper manages the issue and receipt of straw and fodder.

sentences.zh: 獸醫掌療馬病。

translations.literal: Veterinarians are in charge of treating horse ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Veterinarians treat horse diseases.

sentences.zh: 初尚乘局掌六閑馬，後置內外閑廄使，專掌御馬。

translations.literal: Initially the Horse Bureau managed the six leisure [studs'] horses; later Inner and Outer Leisure Stable Commissioners were established to exclusively manage imperial horses.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Horse Bureau managed the six imperial studs; later Inner and Outer Leisure Stable Commissioners were appointed to oversee imperial horses exclusively.

sentences.zh: 開元初，以尚乘局隸閑廄使，乃省尚乘，其左右六閑及局官，並隸閑廄使領之也。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, the Horse Bureau was subordinated to the Leisure Stable Commissioner, and the Horse Bureau was then abolished; the left and right six leisure [studs] and bureau officials all came under the Leisure Stable Commissioner's command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era the Horse Bureau was placed under the Leisure Stable Commissioner and then abolished; the left and right six studs and all bureau officials were placed under the commissioner's authority.

sentences.zh: 進馬舊儀，每日尚乘以廄馬八匹，分為左右廂，立于正殿側宮門外，候仗下即散。

translations.literal: The old ritual for Presenting-Horse officers: daily the Horse Bureau used eight stable horses, divided into left and right wings, standing outside the palace gate beside the main hall; when the guard formation withdrew, they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Presenting-Horse ritual, the Horse Bureau daily deployed eight stable horses in left and right wings outside the palace gate beside the main hall; they dispersed once the guard formation withdrew.

sentences.zh: 若大陳設，即馬在樂懸之北，與大象相次。

translations.literal: At grand array formations, the horses stood north of the suspended bells, alternating with the elephants.
translations.idiomatic: At grand ceremonial formations, the horses were stationed north of the musical bells, arrayed in alternation with the elephants.

sentences.zh: 進馬二人，戎服執鞭，侍立于馬之左，隨馬進退。

translations.literal: Two Presenting-Horse officers in military dress, holding whips, attended standing to the left of the horses, advancing and retreating with them.
translations.idiomatic: Two Presenting-Horse officers in military dress stood to the left of the horses holding whips, advancing and retreating with them.

sentences.zh: 雖名管殿中，其實武職，用資廕簡擇，一如千牛備身。

translations.literal: Although named as managing within the palace hall, in reality it was a military post, used as a source for yin privilege selection, just like the Thousand-Ox Bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Although nominally a palace post, it was in fact a military appointment used as a channel for yin privilege selection, much like the Thousand-Ox Bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，李林甫用事，罷立仗馬，亦省進馬官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, when Li Linfu held power, the standing guard horses were abolished, and the Presenting-Horse officers were also eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao, with Li Linfu in power, the standing guard horses were abolished and the Presenting-Horse officers were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 十二載，楊國忠當政，復立仗馬及進馬官，乾元復省，上元復置也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Yang Guozhong held office, the standing guard horses and Presenting-Horse officers were restored; in Qianyuan they were again eliminated, and in Shangyuan restored again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, under Yang Guozhong, the standing guard horses and Presenting-Horse officers were restored; they were abolished again in Qianyuan and reinstated in Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 尚輦局尚輦局：奉御二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Palanquin Bureau. Palanquin Bureau: two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin Bureau — two Imperial Attendants, upper subordinate fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 直長四人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Four Chief Stewards, lower upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four Chief Stewards, lower upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 尚輦二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Two Chief Palanquin Stewards, lower upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Chief Palanquin Stewards, lower upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 書令史二人，書吏四人，掌扇六人，掌翰二十四人，主輦三十二人，奉輿十二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, four clerical officers, six fan bearers, twenty-four feather-canopy bearers, thirty-two palanquin stewards, twelve carriage attendants, and four storeroom keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, four clerical officers, six fan bearers, twenty-four feather-canopy bearers, thirty-two palanquin stewards, twelve carriage attendants, and four storeroom keepers.

sentences.zh: 奉御掌輿輦，分其次序而辨其名數。

translations.literal: The Imperial Attendant is in charge of palanquins and carriages, assigning their order and distinguishing names and quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Attendants manage palanquins and carriages, set their order of precedence, and keep accounts of names and quantities.

sentences.zh: 直長為之貳。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward is his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Steward serves as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會則陳於廷，大祭祀則陳於廟。

translations.literal: At grand audiences they are displayed in the court; at grand sacrifices they are displayed in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: At grand audiences they are displayed in the court; at grand sacrifices they are displayed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會，則傘二翰一，陳之於廷。

translations.literal: At grand audiences, two umbrellas and one feather canopy are displayed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: At grand audiences, two umbrellas and one feather canopy are displayed in the court.

sentences.zh: 孔雀扇一百五十有六，分居左右。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty-six peacock fans, distributed left and right.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty-six peacock fans are distributed to the left and right.

sentences.zh: 舊翟尾扇，開元年初改為繡孔雀。

translations.literal: Formerly pheasant-tail fans; early in Kaiyuan they were changed to embroidered peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: They were formerly pheasant-tail fans; early in the Kaiyuan era they were replaced with embroidered peacocks.

sentences.zh: 若常聽朝，皆去扇，左右各留其三，以備常儀。

translations.literal: At regular court audiences all fans are removed, three left on each side to serve the regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At regular court audiences all fans are removed except three on each side, retained for the ordinary ceremony.

sentences.zh: 內官妃三人。

translations.literal: Inner court consorts: three posts.
translations.idiomatic: Inner court consorts: three posts.

sentences.zh: 正一品。

translations.literal: Upper first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Upper first rank.

sentences.zh: 《周官》三夫人之位也。

translations.literal: The positions of the Three Consorts in the 《Offices of Zhou》.
translations.idiomatic: These are the positions of the Three Consorts in the 《Offices of Zhou》.

sentences.zh: 隋依周制，立三夫人。

translations.literal: Sui followed the Zhou system and established Three Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Sui followed the Zhou system and established three consorts.

sentences.zh: 武德立四妃：一貴妃，二淑妃，三德妃，四賢妃，位次後之下。

translations.literal: Wude established Four Consorts: first Noble Consort, second Kind Consort, third Virtuous Consort, and fourth Worthy Consort, ranked below the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude four consorts were established: Noble Consort first, Kind Consort second, Virtuous Consort third, and Worthy Consort fourth, all ranked below the Empress.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以為后妃四星，其一正後，不宜更有四妃，乃改定三妃之位：惠妃一，麗妃二，華妃三，下有六儀、美人、才人四等，共二十人以備內官之位也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong held that the four stars of empress and consorts have one as the proper empress, and it was unsuitable to have four consorts; he therefore reformed the Three Consorts' positions: Gracious Consort first, Beautiful Consort second, Splendid Consort third; below them were the Six Prescriptions, Beauties, and Talents in four grades — twenty posts in all to fill the inner court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong held that among the four stars of empress and consort, one is the proper empress and four consorts were inappropriate; he therefore redefined three consort ranks — Gracious Consort first, Beautiful Consort second, Splendid Consort third — with Six Prescriptions, Beauties, and Talents below in four grades, twenty posts in all to staff the inner court.

sentences.zh: 三妃佐後，坐而論婦禮者也。

translations.literal: The Three Consorts assist the Empress, sitting and discussing women's rites.
translations.idiomatic: The three consorts assist the Empress, sitting in council on women's ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 其於內，則無所不統，故不以一務名焉。

translations.literal: Within the inner palace they oversee all matters, hence they are not named for a single duty.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner palace they oversee all affairs, and so are not titled for any single duty.

sentences.zh: 六儀六人，正二品，《周官》九嬪之位也。

translations.literal: Six Prescriptions, six posts, upper second rank — the positions of the Nine Concubines in the 《Offices of Zhou》.
translations.idiomatic: Six Prescriptions, six posts, upper second rank — the positions of the Nine Concubines in the 《Offices of Zhou》.

sentences.zh: 掌教九御四德，率其屬以贊導後之禮儀。

translations.literal: They are in charge of teaching the Nine Imperial Consorts the Four Virtues, leading their subordinates to assist and guide the Empress in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: They teach the Nine Imperial Consorts the Four Virtues and lead their subordinates in assisting and guiding the Empress in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 美人四人，正三品，《周官》二十七世婦之位也。

translations.literal: Beauties, four posts, upper third rank — the positions of the Twenty-seven Worldly Wives in the 《Offices of Zhou》.
translations.idiomatic: Beauties, four posts, upper third rank — the positions of the Twenty-seven Worldly Wives in the 《Offices of Zhou》.

sentences.zh: 掌率女官，修祭祀賓客之事。

translations.literal: In charge of leading female officials and attending to sacrificial rites and guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They lead female officials and oversee sacrificial rites and the reception of guests.

sentences.zh: 才人七人，正四品，《周官》八十一御女之位。

translations.literal: Talents, seven posts, upper fourth rank — the positions of the Eighty-one Imperial Women in the 《Offices of Zhou》.
translations.idiomatic: Talents, seven posts, upper fourth rank — the positions of the Eighty-one Imperial Women in the 《Offices of Zhou》.

sentences.zh: 掌敘宴寢，理絲枲，以獻歲功。

translations.literal: In charge of arranging feasts and bedchamber attendance, managing silk and hemp, and presenting the year's tribute of work.
translations.idiomatic: They arrange feasts and bedchamber attendance, manage silk and hemp production, and present the year's woven tribute.

translations.idiomatic: Six palace Directors, with duties parallel to those of the Six Ministers.

translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace guides the inner court and supervises the staffs of the four bureaus — Records, Announcements, Registers, and Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 凡六尚書物出納文簿，皆印署之。

translations.literal: For all incoming and outgoing ledgers of goods among the Six Directors, they seal and sign them.
translations.idiomatic: All ledgers recording the receipt and issue of goods among the Six Directors are sealed and signed by them.

sentences.zh: 司記掌印，凡宮內諸司簿書出入目錄，審而付行焉。

translations.literal: The Director of Records holds the seal; for all palace bureaus' ledgers and incoming and outgoing inventories, they review and authorize execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Records holds the seal, reviewing and authorizing all ledgers and inventories of incoming and outgoing documents from palace bureaus.

sentences.zh: 典記佐之，女史掌執文書。

translations.literal: The Archivist of Records assists; Female Scribes handle and keep the documents.
translations.idiomatic: The Archivist of Records assists; Female Scribes keep and handle the documents.

sentences.zh: 司言掌宣傳啟奏。

translations.idiomatic: The Director of Announcements proclaims edicts, transmits messages, and presents memorials.

translations.idiomatic: The Director of Registers maintains registers of palace women and their grain stipends.

translations.idiomatic: The Director of Inner Gates manages the inner palace gates and their keys.

translations.literal: The Director of Music leads musicians in practice, deployment of suspended instruments, beating and striking, and advance and withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music leads musicians in rehearsal, the arrangement of suspended instruments, percussion, and ceremonial advance and withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 尚食之職，掌供膳羞品齊之數，總司膳、司醖、司藥、司饎四司之官屬。

translations.literal: The office of Director of Food: in charge of supplying meals, delicacies, and regulated portions, overseeing the personnel of the four bureaus of the Kitchen, Brewing, Pharmacy, and Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Food supplies meals and delicacies in regulated portions, supervising the staffs of the four bureaus — Kitchen, Brewing, Pharmacy, and Provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡進食，先嘗之。

translations.literal: For all food presented, they taste it first.
translations.idiomatic: For all food presented to the court, they taste it first.

sentences.zh: 司膳掌制烹煎和。

translations.literal: The Director of the Kitchen is in charge of preparation, boiling, frying, and seasoning.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Kitchen oversees preparation, boiling, frying, and seasoning.

sentences.zh: 司醖掌酒醴枌飲。

translations.literal: The Director of Brewing is in charge of wine, sweet liquors, and fermented beverages.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Brewing manages wine, sweet liquors, and fermented beverages.

sentences.zh: 司藥掌方藥。

translations.literal: The Director of Pharmacy is in charge of prescriptions and medicaments.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Pharmacy manages prescriptions and medicaments.

sentences.zh: 司饎掌給宮人廩餼飯食、薪炭。

translations.literal: The Director of Provisions is in charge of supplying palace women with grain rations, food, and fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Provisions supplies palace women with grain rations, food, and fuel.

sentences.zh: 尚寢二人，正五品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of the Bedchamber, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of the Bedchamber, upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 司設二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Furnishings, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Furnishings, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典設二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Furnishings, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Furnishings, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌設二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Furnishings, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Furnishings, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史四人。

translations.literal: Four Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Four Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 司輿二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Carriages, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Carriages, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典輿二人，正七品掌輿二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Carriages, upper seventh rank; two Clerks of Carriages, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Carriages, upper seventh rank; two Clerks of Carriages, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史一人。

translations.literal: One Female Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: One Female Scribe.

sentences.zh: 司苑二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Gardens, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Gardens, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典苑二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Gardens, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Gardens, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌苑二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Gardens, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Gardens, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史二人。

translations.literal: Two Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 司燈二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Lamps, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Lamps, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典燈二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Lamps, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Lamps, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌燈二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Lamps, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Lamps, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史二人。

translations.literal: Two Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 尚寢之職，掌燕寢進御之次序，總司設、司輿、司苑、司燈四司之官屬。

translations.literal: The office of Director of the Bedchamber: in charge of the order of attendance at the inner bedchamber, overseeing the personnel of the four bureaus of Furnishings, Carriages, Gardens, and Lamps.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Bedchamber regulates the order of attendance at the inner bedchamber and supervises the staffs of the four bureaus — Furnishings, Carriages, Gardens, and Lamps.

sentences.zh: 司設掌幃帳茵席、掃灑張設。

translations.literal: The Director of Furnishings is in charge of curtains, bedding, mats, sweeping, and setting up furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Furnishings manages curtains, bedding, mats, sweeping, and the arrangement of furnishings.

sentences.zh: 司輿掌輿輦傘扇羽儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Carriages is in charge of palanquins, carriages, umbrellas, fans, and feathered standards.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Carriages manages palanquins, carriages, umbrellas, fans, and feathered standards.

sentences.zh: 司苑掌園苑種植蔬果。

translations.literal: The Director of Gardens is in charge of planting fruits and vegetables in the palace gardens.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Gardens oversees the planting of fruits and vegetables in the palace gardens.

sentences.zh: 司燈掌燈燭。

translations.literal: The Director of Lamps is in charge of lamps and candles.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Lamps manages lamps and candles.

sentences.zh: 尚功二人，正五品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Works, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Works, upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 司制二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Manufacture, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Manufacture, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典制二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Manufacture, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Manufacture, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌制二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Manufacture, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Manufacture, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史二人。

translations.literal: Two Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 司珍二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Treasures, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Treasures, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典珍二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Treasures, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Treasures, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌珍二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Treasures, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Treasures, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史六人。

translations.literal: Six Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Six Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 司彩二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Dyes and Colors, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Dyes and Colors, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典彩二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Dyes and Colors, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Dyes and Colors, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌彩二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Dyes and Colors, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Dyes and Colors, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史二人。

translations.literal: Two Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 司計二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Accounts, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Accounts, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典計二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Accounts, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Accounts, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌計二人，正八品。

translations.literal: Two Clerks of Accounts, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Clerks of Accounts, upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 女史二人。

translations.literal: Two Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Two Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 尚功之職，掌女功之程課，總司制、司珍、司彩、司計四司之官屬。

translations.literal: The office of Director of Works: in charge of quotas and assessments for women's craftwork, overseeing the personnel of the four bureaus of Manufacture, Treasures, Dyes and Colors, and Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Works sets quotas and assesses women's craftwork, supervising the staffs of the four bureaus — Manufacture, Treasures, Dyes and Colors, and Accounts.

sentences.zh: 司制掌衣服裁縫。

translations.literal: The Director of Manufacture is in charge of cutting and sewing garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Manufacture oversees the cutting and sewing of garments.

sentences.zh: 司珍掌寶貨。

translations.literal: The Director of Treasures is in charge of precious goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Treasures manages precious goods.

sentences.zh: 司彩掌繒錦絲枲之事。

translations.literal: The Director of Dyes and Colors is in charge of silk brocades, silk thread, and hemp fiber.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Dyes and Colors manages silk brocades, silk thread, and hemp fiber.

sentences.zh: 司計掌支度衣服、飲食、薪炭。

translations.literal: The Director of Accounts is in charge of allotments for clothing, food, and fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Accounts manages allotments for clothing, food, and fuel.

sentences.zh: 宮正一人，正五品。

translations.literal: One Palace Rectifier, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Palace Rectifier, upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 司正二人，正六品。

translations.literal: Two Directors of Rectification, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Directors of Rectification, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 典正二人，正七品。

translations.literal: Two Archivists of Rectification, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Archivists of Rectification, upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 女史四人。

translations.literal: Four Female Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Four Female Scribes.

sentences.zh: 宮正之職，掌戒令、糾禁、謫罰之事。

translations.literal: The office of Palace Rectifier: in charge of admonitions, prohibitions, and matters of discipline and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Rectifier enforces admonitions and prohibitions and handles discipline and punishment.

sentences.zh: 司正、典正佐之。

translations.literal: The Directors and Archivists of Rectification assist.
translations.idiomatic: The Directors and Archivists of Rectification assist in these duties.

sentences.zh: 右唐制定宮官六尚書、二十四司職事官，以備內職之數。

translations.literal: The foregoing is the Tang regulation establishing the six palace directors, twenty-four bureaus, and functional offices to complete the roster of inner-court posts.
translations.idiomatic: The foregoing is the Tang regulation establishing six palace directors, twenty-four bureaus, and their functional offices to complete the roster of inner-court posts.

sentences.zh: 內侍省內侍省《星經》有宦者四星，在天市垣，帝坐之西。

translations.literal: Palace Eunuch Directorate. The Palace Eunuch Directorate: the 《Star Classic》 records four stars associated with eunuchs, within the Celestial Market Enclosure west of the Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Eunuch Directorate. The 《Star Classic》 places four stars associated with eunuchs within the Celestial Market Enclosure, west of the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 《周官》有巷伯、寺人之職，皆內官也。

translations.literal: The 《Offices of Zhou》 has the posts of the Lane Steward and Palace Attendant — all are inner-court offices.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Offices of Zhou》 lists the Lane Steward and Palace Attendant — both are inner-court offices.

sentences.zh: 前漢宮官，多用士人，後漢始用宦者為宮官。

translations.literal: In Former Han, palace offices mostly employed gentlemen; Later Han first employed eunuchs as palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han mostly filled palace offices with gentlemen; Later Han was the first to appoint eunuchs as palace officials.

sentences.zh: 晉置大長秋卿為後宮官，以宦者為之。

translations.literal: Jin established the Grand Director of Autumn as a rear-palace office, filled by eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin established the Grand Director of Autumn as a rear-palace office and filled it with eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 隋為內侍省，煬帝改為長秋監。

translations.literal: Under Sui it was the Palace Eunuch Directorate; Emperor Yang changed it to the Autumn Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui it was the Palace Eunuch Directorate; Emperor Yang renamed it the Autumn Superintendency.

sentences.zh: 武德復為內侍。

translations.literal: Wude restored the name Palace Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude era restored the name Palace Eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為內侍監，光宅改為司宮臺，神龍復為內侍省也。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to the Eunuch Superintendency; Guangzhai changed it to the Palace Office Terrace; Shenlong restored the Palace Eunuch Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it the Eunuch Superintendency; Guangzhai renamed it the Palace Office Terrace; Shenlong restored the Palace Eunuch Directorate.

sentences.zh: 內侍四員。

translations.literal: Four Palace Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Four Palace Eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 從四品上。

translations.literal: Upper lower fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Upper lower fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏曰長秋卿，梁曰大長秋，北齊曰中侍中，後周曰司內上士，隋曰內侍，置二人。

translations.literal: Under Han and Wei it was called Director of Autumn; under Liang, Grand Director of Autumn; under Northern Qi, Palace Vice Attendant; under Later Zhou, Senior Palace Master; under Sui, Palace Eunuch — two posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei called it Director of Autumn; Liang called it Grand Director of Autumn; Northern Qi called it Palace Vice Attendant; Later Zhou called it Senior Palace Master; Sui called it Palace Eunuch and established two posts.

sentences.zh: 煬帝曰長秋令，正四品。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang styled it Director of Autumn, upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang styled the office Director of Autumn, upper fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 武德復為中侍。

translations.literal: Wude restored the title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude era restored the title Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 中官之貴，極於此矣。

translations.literal: Among inner-court officials, none ranks higher.
translations.idiomatic: Among inner-court officials, none outranked this post.

sentences.zh: 若有殊勳懋績，則有拜大將軍者，仍兼內侍之官。

translations.literal: Those with exceptional merit might be appointed General-in-Chief while retaining the palace eunuch office.
translations.idiomatic: Men of exceptional merit might be appointed General-in-Chief while still holding the palace eunuch office.

sentences.zh: 德宗置左、右神策、威遠等禁兵，命中官掌之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong established the Left and Right Divine Stratagem Armies, the Weiyuan Army, and other palace guards, assigning eunuchs to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong established the Left and Right Divine Stratagem Armies, the Weiyuan Army, and other palace guards, placing eunuchs in command.

sentences.zh: 每軍置中尉一人，宦者為之。

translations.literal: Each army had one Army Commander, a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Army Commander, always a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 自李輔國、魚朝恩之後，京師兵柄，歸於內官，號左、右軍中尉。

translations.literal: After Li Fuguo and Yu Chao'en, control of the capital armies passed to eunuchs, styled the Left and Right Army Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Fuguo and Yu Chao'en, control of the capital armies passed to eunuchs styled the Left and Right Army Commanders.

sentences.zh: 將兵於外者，謂之觀軍容使。

translations.literal: Those commanding troops abroad were called Military Observers.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs commanding troops in the field were called Military Observers.

sentences.zh: 而天下軍鎮節度使，皆內官一人監之，事具《宦者傳》也。

translations.literal: Every military commissioner and frontier command throughout the realm had a eunuch supervisor; the details are recorded in the 《Biographies of Eunuchs》.
translations.idiomatic: Every military commissioner and frontier command throughout the realm had a eunuch supervisor; the details are given in the 《Biographies of Eunuchs》.

sentences.zh: 內常侍六人。

translations.literal: Six Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Six Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 正五品下。

translations.literal: Lower upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 漢代謂之中常侍。

translations.literal: Under Han it was called Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han the office was called Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 內侍之職，掌在內侍奉出入宮掖宣傳之事，總掖廷、宮闈、奚官、內僕、內府五局之官屬。

translations.literal: The office of Palace Eunuch is in charge of attending within the palace, entering and leaving the inner precincts, and conveying announcements, overseeing the personnel of the five bureaus of the Rear Palace, Inner Gate, Wards Office, Inner Servants, and Inner Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Eunuch attends within the palace, enters and leaves the inner precincts, and conveys announcements, supervising the staffs of the five bureaus — Rear Palace, Inner Gate, Wards Office, Inner Servants, and Inner Treasury.

sentences.zh: 內常侍為之貳。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary serve as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendants-in-Ordinary serve as their deputies.

sentences.zh: 凡皇后祭先蠶，則相儀。

translations.literal: Whenever the empress sacrifices to the Silkworm Goddess, they assist in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the empress sacrifices to the Silkworm Goddess, they assist in the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 後出，則為之夾引。

translations.literal: When she goes out, they walk on either side to guide her.
translations.idiomatic: When she goes out, they walk on either side to guide her.

sentences.zh: 內給事八人，從五品下。

translations.literal: Eight Palace Provisioners, lower lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Palace Provisioners, lower lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Two Principal Clerks, lower lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two Principal Clerks, lower lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 令史八人，書令史十六人。

translations.literal: Eight Recorder Clerks; sixteen Document Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Recorder Clerks; sixteen Document Clerks.

sentences.zh: 內給事掌判省事。

translations.literal: The Palace Provisioners supervise handling of office business.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Provisioners supervise the handling of office business.

sentences.zh: 凡元正、冬至群臣朝賀中宮，則出入宣傳。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice, when officials attend court to congratulate the Central Palace, they enter and leave to convey announcements.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice, when officials attend court to congratulate the empress, they enter and leave to convey announcements.

sentences.zh: 凡宮人衣服費用，則具其品秩，計其多少，春秋二時，宣送中書。

translations.literal: For all palace women's clothing expenses, they itemize rank and calculate quantities, and in spring and autumn transmit this to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For all palace women's clothing expenses, they itemize rank, calculate quantities, and in spring and autumn transmit the accounts to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 內謁者監六人，正六品下。

translations.literal: Six Supervisors of Palace Ushers, lower upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Six Supervisors of Palace Ushers, lower upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 內謁者十二人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Twelve Palace Ushers, lower lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Palace Ushers, lower lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 內寺伯二人。

translations.literal: Two Palace Ward Stewards.
translations.idiomatic: Two Palace Ward Stewards.

sentences.zh: 正七品下。

translations.literal: Lower upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 內謁者監掌內宣傳。

translations.literal: The Supervisors of Palace Ushers are in charge of inner-court announcements.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisors of Palace Ushers manage inner-court announcements.

sentences.zh: 凡諸親命婦朝會，所司籍其人數，送內侍省。

translations.literal: For all imperial kinswomen and titled ladies attending court assemblies, the responsible office registers their numbers and sends them to the Palace Eunuch Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: For all imperial kinswomen and titled ladies attending court assemblies, the responsible office registers their numbers and forwards them to the Palace Eunuch Directorate.

sentences.zh: 內謁者掌諸親命婦朝集班位。

translations.literal: The Palace Ushers manage the formation and seating of imperial kinswomen and titled ladies at court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Ushers arrange the formation and seating of imperial kinswomen and titled ladies at court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 內寺伯掌糾察諸不法之事。

translations.literal: The Palace Ward Stewards are in charge of investigating all unlawful conduct.
